title: Downloadable invoice slices - UX proposal and backlog
content:
Context:

This doc captures a focused UX proposal and grooming notes for a new console flow: Downloadable invoice slices. The goal: let customers export arbitrary slices of invoicing/billing data tied to cost allocation (cost centers, tags, projects), budgets and alert contexts, and make those exports predictable, audit-friendly, and resumable for large datasets.

Why we need this (user problems):
- Finance teams want exports scoped to cost centers for reconciling chargebacks without pulling full invoice payloads.
- Platform teams need scheduled extracts for downstream analytics (warehouse) and to detect budget regressions early.
- Customers running Dedicated/Private need S3-compatible delivery, hosted customers may prefer signed URLs.
- Current console only has coarse invoice downloads (per-month zip) which forces expensive post-processing.

High-level proposal:
- New console flow: Billing > Exports > New export > "Invoice slice"
- Slice dimensions: time window (start/end), allocation filters (cost centers, tags, org units), models used, routes, account type (hosted/dedicated/private), currency preference
- Output formats: CSV (flat), CSV-raw-events (row per token/request), JSONL (event-based), Parquet (columnar for warehouse)
- Delivery options: immediate download (signed URL), push to S3 (customer bucket or Redwood-managed), push to BigQuery/GCS via connector (GA later)
- Scheduling: one-off, daily/weekly, monthly cadence with retention policy and rotation
- Permissions: RBAC gates by role (billing-admin, finance-reader). Export preview limited to 2 weeks for non-admins to prevent accidental large queries.

Wireframe + microcopy (sketch):
- Screen 1: Export details (title, owner, description)
  * Input: "Export name" (required)
  * Microcopy: "Use clear names (e.g. 'Q1-2026 - USA Cost Centers') for bookkeeping and scheduled runs. Exports are immutable once created."
- Screen 2: Scope filters (multi-panel)
  * Time range picker (start/end) with quick presets: last 7/30/90/365 days, billing month
  * Allocation selector: typeahead multi-select for cost center tags, label mapping, ad-hoc tag expressions (tag:key=value)
  * Model selector: 'All models' or pick list (runnable per model to include model metadata columns)
  * Route selector: checkboxes for API routes (chat, embeddings, rerank)
  * Currency: drop-down with conversion note: "Exports standardize values using the billing currency at invoice time unless 'convert to account currency' is selected."
- Screen 3: Format & delivery
  * Format radio: CSV | JSONL | Parquet
  * Columns chooser: checkboxes for optional columns (invoice_id, line_item_id, usage_window_start, usage_window_end, quantity, unit_price, model, route, cost_center_tag, raw_prompt_hash)
  * Delivery: Immediate download (signed URL) | Push to S3 (supply bucket + prefix) | Schedule
  * Microcopy: "Parquet recommended for large exports and warehouse loads. CSV works for ad-hoc reconciliation. JSONL preserves nested usage metadata."
- Screen 4: Scheduling and retention
  * Schedule: one-off / daily / weekly / monthly, timezone selector, retry policy
  * Retention: keep exports for 30/90/365 days or custom. Optionally auto-rotate older exports to Glacier-like low-cost storage (Redwood-managed).
- Screen 5: Review & create
  * Estimated size & cost: show sample preview: row estimate and estimated storage/egress cost. Warning for >100k rows for immediate download.
  * CTA: Create export (button) and Cancel

Preflight and export execution behavior:
- Preflight validates filters and calculates approximate row count and estimated output size. If preflight fails (invalid tag mapping, missing permission, bucket write failed), show helpful actionable error.
- Exports are performed as jobs with an export-id. Jobs are resumable and chunked; each chunk stored as part file (slice_0001.csv, slice_0002.csv).
- For immediate downloads, we stream a zip of current completed chunks and continue background streaming for large sets; signed URLs are short-lived (24h) and multiple requests are supported to pick up later chunks.
- For push-to-S3, job writes to target prefix using idempotent keys and a manifest.json summarizing parts (checksum, row count).
- Audit trail: each export job writes metadata to the export index (who created, filters, timestamp, job status). Console shows job logs and links to sample rows for quick verification.

Edge cases & decisions to surface in grooming:
- Currency & credits: how to represent refunds/credits? Should we produce invoice-net vs invoice-gross rows? Proposal: export both a raw event row (gross) and an aggregation row (net per invoice) if customer selects 'include settlements'.
- Tag mapping drift: tags in usage events might change over time. Exports should include both resolved cost_center and raw tag key for forensic backfill.
- Timezone normalization: store usage timestamps in UTC and present an option to convert to account timezone on export.
- Large historical exports: throttle or require special approval for exports > 1M rows for hosted customers to avoid noisy queries. For Dedicated/Private, provide a 'bulk export' flow via support/solutions-eng.
- PII: mask prompt texts unless customer opts-in explicitly (opt-in must be auditable).

Backlog (groomed items with priority & rough sizing):
1) EXPORT-001: Basic one-off invoice slice UI (filters, CSV immediate download) - P0 - 3 SP
2) EXPORT-002: Preflight row estimate & cost approximation - P0 - 2 SP
3) EXPORT-003: Push-to-S3 delivery with manifest + idempotency - P0 - 5 SP
4) EXPORT-004: Scheduled exports / retention controls - P1 - 5 SP
5) EXPORT-005: Parquet & JSONL support + column chooser - P1 - 3 SP
6) EXPORT-006: RBAC + export preview limits - P1 - 2 SP
7) EXPORT-007: Audit logs + console job view (streamed logs) - P1 - 3 SP
8) EXPORT-008: Currency conversion + credit handling rules - P2 - 5 SP
9) EXPORT-009: Dedicated/Private S3 connector auth patterns (IAM role delegation) - P0 for Dedicated - 4 SP
10) EXPORT-010: Large-historical export flow + support playbook - P2 - 2 SP

Acceptance criteria (for EXPORT-001 / P0):
- Users can create an invoice-slice export with time range and allocation filters and immediately download a CSV containing columns: invoice_id, usage_start, usage_end, quantity, unit_price, cost_center_tag, model
- Preflight must return an estimated row count within 20% accuracy for datasets <100k rows
- Console shows export job in activity list with status (running, completed, failed)
- Downloaded CSV must match the schema selected and include a header row with column names
- Only users with billing-admin or export-create privileges can create/export (others see disabled controls with tooltip)

Security, compliance, and privacy notes:
- For hosted customers we do not include full prompt text by default. Provide explicit checkbox: "Include prompt text (sensitive)" which requires 2-person approval for scheduled exports.
- All push-to-customer-bucket flows require an encrypted transfer (TLS) and server-side encryption on target (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS) depending on customer preference.
- Exports metadata (filters, created_by, created_at, job metadata) must be retained for audit for 365 days by default.

Telemetry & observability requirements:
- Export metrics: job_count, job_duration, row_count, bytes_written, delivery_failures, preflight_estimate_accuracy
- Error classification for logs: validation_errors, permission_errors, delivery_errors, processing_errors
- Console should surface recent failed exports with one-click rerun and link to logs.

Beta rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (alpha internal + select customers): Basic one-off CSV immediate download + S3 push for Dedicated customers (Q1 2026)
- Phase 2: Scheduling, retention, JSONL/Parquet support (Q2 2026)
- Phase 3: Connectors (BigQuery/GCS), advanced scheduling (cron expressions), and SLA for export delivery (Q3 2026)

Open questions for next grooming session:
- Should exports support "snapshot at invoice close" vs raw usage events? (impacts row semantics and credit handling)
- How strict is the CSV schema vs evolving fields (we will need a version field on manifest if we change columns)
- Exact approval workflow for scheduled exports that include sensitive data (who signs off? Solutions-eng?)

Quick notes from Slack discussion (synthesized):
- Marco: prefer manifest.json with checksums + part list (helps resumption)
- Jingwen: need to ensure mapping between tags and cost_center ids is stable; include mapping table in export
- Avery: add UI guardrails to prevent accidental exports > 500k rows without explicit confirmation

Next steps (action items):
- Product: finalize acceptance criteria (Priya) and create JIRA epic (EXPORT-Epic-Downloadable-Slices)
- Eng: spike on preflight estimation algorithm + cost estimator (Marco + Jingwen), 1 week
- SRE/Security: draft S3 delivery security checklist and KMS options (Avery)
- Design: produce high-fidelity mockups for the 5 screens + microcopy (2 sprints)

Appendix: sample CSV row (columns currently proposed)
invoice_id, invoice_date, line_item_id, usage_start, usage_end, model, route, quantity, unit_price, currency, cost_center_tag, raw_tag_expression, prompt_hash
inv_2026_0001,2026-01-31,line_1234,2026-01-15T12:34:00Z,2026-01-15T12:34:30Z,gpt-6-std,chat,1,0.020,USD,cc-website,env=prod;team=payments,hash_abc123
